question: Does the current async public cancel tool block unrelated work on its event loop while its synchronous owned-session cleanup boundary is delayed?
runtime: Windows host; Python multiprocessing spawn for the owned session; repository Fake X owner fixture; no X server, Xlib server operation, physical input, WSL, WSLc, Docker, or external model

no-injected-cleanup-delay.expectation: standard caller returns cancellation cleanup UNKNOWN, denies replay, and event-loop heartbeat is delayed by the existing synchronous control/retirement path

injected-cleanup-boundary-delay.expectation: standard caller response and event-loop heartbeat include both injected delays; cleanup remains UNKNOWN and replay is denied

frozen_inputs.action: one CTRL+a chord; fake owner blocks in its sync until parent retirement
frozen_inputs.fake_x_cleanup: disconnect and release stage results are deterministic injected receipts; no physical release inference

measurements: cancel_tool_elapsed_ms from immediately before public MCP tool invocation through returned metadata
maximum event-loop heartbeat gap in the interval beginning immediately before cancel invocation and ending immediately after it
cancel status, release_confirmed, cleanup_status, task_success, replay_allowed
owner retirement receipt, obligation snapshot and terminal standard-caller result

decision.evidence_rule: All six trials must retain complete records and report cleanup UNKNOWN, release_confirmed=false, task_success=null and replay_allowed=false. Compare observed per-arm latency distributions; no claim of a release guarantee is permitted.
decision.scope_limit: Injected delays model synchronous waiting at cleanup boundaries; they are not actual Process.start delays, XRes wire calls, X11, physical input, or live release. This probe cannot validate the proposed architecture or its budgets.
